title: Generic residual nesting for a strict negative extremal Clifford cluster
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes, meaning that at every singular closed point its completed local $k$-algebra is $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Write $h^i(X,F)=\dim_kH^i(X,F)$ for Zariski module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Assume that for every decomposition $X=A\cup B$ into nonempty reduced unions of components with no common component, $\dim_k\Gamma(A\times_XB,\mathcal O_{A\times_XB})\ge2$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $p_a(X)=1-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. Let $S\subseteq X$ be a subcanonical zero-dimensional closed subscheme, with ideal $I_S$ and splitting index $r(S)$ in [def-sfb-subcanonical-splitting-index]. Write $F_S=I_S\otimes\omega_X$, $V_S=H^0(X,F_S)$, $\ell(S)=\dim_k\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$ and $c(S)=2p_a(X)-\ell(S)-2\dim_kV_S$. Regard $V_S$ as a subspace of $H^0(X,\omega_X)$. Fix $R\in\mathbf N$. Assume $r(S)\le R$, $c(S)<0$, and that for every subcanonical cluster $U\subseteq X$ with $r(U)\le R$ one has $c(S)\le c(U)$; among the clusters with $r(U)\le R$ and $c(U)=c(S)$ assume $\ell(S)\ge\ell(U)$. Let $s\in V_S$ be nonzero at every component generic point, let $S^*$ be its residual [lem-sfb-subcanonical-residual-duality], and let $U=S\cup S^*$ denote the scheme-theoretic union, defined by $I_U=I_S\cap I_{S^*}$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Assume explicitly that $U$ is subcanonical and $r(U)\le R$. Then $S^*\subseteq S$ as closed subschemes. No condition on $r(S^*)$ or on the splitting index of $S\cap S^*$ is imposed; $s$ need not be general once the union hypothesis holds. No Cartier condition on $S$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $T=S^*$, $D=S\cap T$ with $I_D=I_S+I_T$, and $v(Z)=h^0(X,I_Z\otimes\omega_X)$. The residual-duality theorem applies to $S$ with the specified generically nonzero section $s$: it gives that $T$ is subcanonical and that taking its residual with the same $s$ gives $S$. The inclusion $F_S\hookrightarrow\omega_X$ is a section of $\mathcal Hom(F_S,\omega_X)$ whose value at $s$ is $s$; therefore $s\in V_T$. Consequently $s\in V_U\subseteq V_D$ and is generically nonzero in both. Thus $D$ is subcanonical, and all four clusters admit residuals with respect to this same $s$. Their section spaces and lengths are finite by the same theorem.

source.place: Lemma 3.1, printed p.235: union/intersection argument, specialized to a single residual pair; elementary details supplied by the agent.

proof.text: We check directly that the residual of $D$ is $U$. Work locally, trivializing the invertible module $\omega_X$. The identities $F_D=F_S+F_T$ and $F_U=F_S\cap F_T$ follow by adding and intersecting the defining ideals. A map $F_D\to\omega_X$ restricts to maps on $F_S,F_T$ with the same value at $s$, so its evaluation lies in the intersection of their evaluation images. Conversely, let $y$ belong to both images, with maps $\phi:F_S\to\omega_X$ and $\psi:F_T\to\omega_X$ evaluating to $y$. Their restrictions to $F_U$ agree: their difference evaluates to zero at $s$, and the residual theorem for the subcanonical cluster $U$ says evaluation on $\mathcal Hom(F_U,\omega_X)$ is injective. Hence $a+b\mapsto\phi(a)+\psi(b)$ is a well-defined map on $F_D=F_S+F_T$ evaluating to $y$. The local descended maps agree on overlaps because evaluation for $D$ is injective as well. The evaluation image for $D$ is therefore the intersection of the images for $S,T$, namely $F_T\cap F_S=F_U$, by residual involutivity. Uniqueness in the residual theorem identifies $D^*=U$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1, printed p.235: union/intersection argument, specialized to a single residual pair; elementary details supplied by the agent.

proof.text:
The addition map $V_S\oplus V_T\to V_D$, $(a,b)\mapsto a+b$, has kernel $\{(a,-a):a\in V_U\}$, since $F_U=F_S\cap F_T$. Rank-nullity gives $v(S)+v(T)\le v(U)+v(D)$; it does not assert surjectivity onto $V_D$. Residual duality for the pairs $(S,T)$ and $(D,U)$ gives
$$\ell(S)+\ell(T)=2p_a(X)-2=\ell(D)+\ell(U),\qquad c(T)=c(S),\qquad c(D)=c(U).$$
Substitution in $c(Z)=2p_a(X)-\ell(Z)-2v(Z)$ yields $2c(U)=c(U)+c(D)\le c(S)+c(T)=2c(S)$. Thus $c(U)\le c(S)$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1, printed p.235: union/intersection argument, specialized to a single residual pair; elementary details supplied by the agent.

proof.text: The assumed subcanonicity and bound $r(U)\le R$ permit the extremal comparison with $U$, giving $c(S)\le c(U)$. Together with the previous step this gives equality. The maximal-length assumption among minimizers then gives $\ell(U)\le\ell(S)$. Neither comparison involves $r(T)$ or $r(D)$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1, printed p.235: union/intersection argument, specialized to a single residual pair; elementary details supplied by the agent.

proof.text:
For the final length comparison, $X$ is Noetherian: projectivity implies properness, hence finite type over $k$, and the finite-type Noetherian theorem applies to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$). A closed subscheme of $X$ is Noetherian: locally its ring is a quotient of a Noetherian ring and its underlying space is a closed subspace of the Noetherian space. In particular $U$ is Noetherian. The zero-dimensional Noetherian theorem makes $|U|$ finite discrete. On this space a sheaf is the product of its sections on the finitely many singleton opens, each such section module being the stalk. The closed inclusion $S\subseteq U$ gives a surjection on every structure-sheaf stalk, hence a surjection
$$\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S).$$
Both are finite-dimensional, so $\ell(S)\le\ell(U)$.

source.place: Tag 0AAX, lemma-locally-Noetherian-dimension-0; finite-discrete sections computed directly. Finite type over a Noetherian base is morphisms.tex Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; projective proper is Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper.

proof.text: We have $\ell(S)=\ell(U)$. The preceding surjection of finite-dimensional $k$-spaces is therefore an isomorphism. In the singleton-open decomposition, each stalk kernel is zero; thus the ideal $I_S/I_U$ on $U$ is zero. It follows that $I_U=I_S$, so $U=S$ as closed subschemes. Since $T\subseteq U$ by the defining ideal intersection, $S^*=T\subseteq S$. This uses equality of ideals, including nilpotents, and imposes no Cartier condition.
